analysis: Examined head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 29714-31296). The file is a public golden-vector fixture with synthetic prompts ("Public followup", "Public synthetic cache-parity input", "Nulls must disappear", etc.), token IDs, prompt_contract_id values and prefix-cache chain hashes. It contains no secrets, keys, tokens, attestation material or real consumer data, so there is no A-001 exposure. The file_changes patch shows an update to expected token counts, block-boundary chain hashes and token IDs for a Qwen-style vector, and adds an additional_context enable_thinking=false field in template_input. These are test-vector changes only. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not review the remaining changed ranges (for example around lines 3020-3926, 43739, 52354). The visible units are unchanged-looking fixture content with no executable code, authorization, encryption or attestation behavior. Relevant threat context is T-041 (the prefix-cache chain hash and TTFT oracle), which concerns cache-key derivation. The fixture only pins expected hashes, and I saw no weakening of the hash chain or block size (256-token boundaries remain). One integration question remains: whether the prompt-contract ID and chain hash derivation in the provider Swift code and the coordinator was changed consistently with these vectors, for example the template additional_context handling. That is outside the supplied source. No concrete security regression is identified from these units, and the cross-implementation parity contract was not verifiable here.
